question: Who discovered the law of octaves and compared this to the octaves found in music?
solution:
The correct answer is __**John Newlands**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **John Newlands**, an English scientist, discovered the law of octaves and compared this to the octaves found in music.
 
• The law of octaves found to be applicable up to the element Calcium (Ca).__
 
• He started with the element having the lowest atomic mass (hydrogen) and ended at thorium which was the 56th element.
 
• He found that every eighth element has properties similar to that of the first.
 
• He compared this to the octaves found in music.
 
• Therefore, he called it the ‘Law of Octaves’ and hence it is known as ‘Newlands’ Law of Octaves’.
 
• It was found that the Law of Octaves was applicable only upto calcium,
 __
 
• as after calcium every eighth element did not possess properties similar to that of the first.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dmitri Mendeléev**

 
 
• The periodic table was discovered by __Dimitri Ivanovich Mendeleev__.__
 
• The periodic table of Mendeleev was based on the increasing order of atomic mass.
 
• Dmitri Mendeleev is also known as the father of the periodic table.
 
 
 
• **Johann Dobereiner**
 
 
• **T​**he German chemist, Johann Dobereiner in the early 1800s was the** first t**o consider the idea of trends among properties of elements.
 
• By 1829 he noted a similarity among the physical and chemical properties of several groups of three elements (Triads).
 
 
 
• **Johann Jakob Balmer**
 
 
• **​He​** Discovered a mathematical formula predicting wavelengths of hydrogen spectral lines (1885)
 
• He also Derived an **empirical equation for calculating hydrogen spectrum wavelengths.**
